Common Rehabilitation Billing Problems

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

3-hour therapy rule not met on some admission days, creating IRF compliance exposure.

PMEX tracks documented therapy minutes per day per patient and flags days where the 3-hour threshold is not met.

FIM scores entered incorrectly, placing the patient in a lower-paying CMG than clinical status supports.

PMEX reviews FIM score documentation against the clinical record before submitting the CMG for IRF PPS assignment.

IRF admission criteria not fully documented, creating denial exposure on Medicare audit.

PMEX confirms the required pre-admission screening documentation is complete before the IRF claim is submitted.

Outpatient rehab therapy cap exceeded without KX modifier, claims denied automatically.

PMEX tracks therapy utilization per patient per benefit year and applies KX modifier before the cap is reached.

Outpatient rehab E/M not billed on evaluation days when a separately identifiable evaluation was performed.

PMEX identifies evaluation-day encounters and submits the correct evaluation code alongside the therapy codes.

IRF discharge claim not submitted within the Medicare timely filing window.

PMEX tracks IRF discharge dates and confirms claims are submitted within the Medicare timely filing period.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in Rehabilitation Billing

Rehabilitation facilities lose 14 to 24 percent of revenue to 3-hour rule compliance failures, FIM scoring errors, and therapy cap violations.

PATTERN 01

IRF Denied, 3-Hour Rule Not Met

Medicare audit of IRF admission. On 3 of 15 admission days, documented therapy minutes fall below 3 hours. Medicare requires at least 3 hours of therapy per day on at least 5 days per week. Admission does not meet IRF criteria. Claim recouped. $12,000 to $22,000 per IRF stay at risk.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX monitors documented therapy minutes per day per patient throughout the IRF stay, flagging days where total minutes are below the 3-hour threshold so the clinical team can address documentation or scheduling before the claim is submitted.

PATTERN 02

FIM Score Inaccurate, Lower CMG Assigned

Patient admitted post-stroke. FIM scores entered at the time of admission reflect function below the patient's actual status. CMG assigned is lower than the accurate score would support. IRF PPS payment reduced by $800 to $1,400 per stay from one FIM documentation error.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX reviews FIM scores against the clinical documentation before the CMG is assigned. When FIM entries appear inconsistent with the documented clinical status, PMEX flags the scores for clinical review before the IRF PPS calculation is finalized.

PATTERN 03

Outpatient Rehab Cap Exceeded, KX Modifier Missing

Medicare patient reaches the annual therapy cap ($2,330 combined PT and OT). Next therapy visit submitted without KX modifier. Medicare denies automatically. KX modifier attests that services above the cap are medically necessary. Revenue lost with no appeal pathway.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX tracks therapy utilization per Medicare patient against the annual cap threshold and automatically applies KX modifier to all claims at or above the cap with supporting medical necessity documentation confirmed in the clinical notes.

Questions

Rehabilitation Billing Questions Answered

Medicare requires that IRF patients receive at least 3 hours of therapy per day on at least 5 days per week. Failure to meet this threshold can result in denial of the IRF admission on audit. We track therapy minutes daily.

The Functional Independence Measure (FIM) assesses a patient's level of independence across 18 functional areas. FIM scores determine the Case Mix Group (CMG), which determines the IRF PPS payment rate. Accurate scoring is critical to correct reimbursement.

Medicare requires a pre-admission screening, post-admission physician evaluation within 24 hours, an individualized overall plan of care within 4 days, and documentation of the patient's ability to participate in intensive therapy.

Medicare limits combined PT and OT to $2,330 per year. Speech therapy has a separate $2,330 cap. Services above the cap are covered when medically necessary with the KX modifier. We track cap utilization per patient.

Yes. We manage IRF PPS facility billing and outpatient therapy professional fee billing under one RCM workflow.
